question.prompt: Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A = (3, 0),\) \(B = (0, 3),\) and \(C,\) where \(C\) is on the line \(x + y = 7.\) What is the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

solutions.explanation:
Both \(A=(3,0)\) and \(B=(0,3)\) lie on \(x+y=3\), so this is the line containing \(AB\). Written as \(y=-x+3\) and \(y=-x+7\), the two lines have the same slope and different intercepts, so they are parallel.

Parallel lines have constant perpendicular separation. Therefore every allowed position of \(C\) gives the same height above the fixed base \(AB\), and hence the same triangle area.

Choose \(D=(7,0)\), which lies on \(x+y=7\). Triangle \(ABD\) has the same area as triangle \(ABC\). For triangle \(ABD\), use \(AD\) as the base: it lies on the \(x\)-axis and has length \(7-3=4\). The corresponding height from \(B=(0,3)\) is \(3\). Thus
\[
[ABC]=[ABD]=\frac12\cdot4\cdot3=\boxed{6},
\]
choice A.
